test_title: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On: 10 Sept, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Study the given bar-graph and answer the question that follows.

The bar-graph shows the sales of books (in thousands) from six branches (B1, B2, B3, B4, B5 and B6) of a publishing

company during two consecutive years 2000 and 2001.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/421d0789c33b0aff8ff256a2f6604e99bce65ba9dba1a98f5dc31595bed2b83c.png] 

The total sales of branch B6 for both the years is what percentage of the total sales of branch B3 for both the years (correct up to two decimal places)?
solution:
**Given:**

Sales of branch B6 in 2000 = 70,000

Sales of branch B6 in 2001 = 80,000

Total sales of B6 = 70,000 + 80,000 = 150,000

Sales of branch B3 in 2000 = 95,000

Sales of branch B3 in 2001 = 110,000

Total sales of B3 = 95,000 + 110,000 = 205,000

**Formula used:**

Percentage = dfrac{{Total sales of B6}}{{Total sales of B3}} times 100

**Calculation:**

Percentage = dfrac{150,000}{205,000} times 100 

⇒ Percentage =&
nbsp;73.17%

**∴ The total sales of branch B6 for both years is 73.17% of the total sales of branch B3 for both years.**
